items.excerpt: A health system is replacing the human second reader in screening mammography with an AI model — an AI system standing in for a radiologist in a live screening pathway, not an assistive add-on.
items.rationale: A live clinical deployment where AI replaces a clinician in the pathway rather than assisting one — the clearest example of medical AI actually reaching patients.

items.excerpt: Utah expanded its healthcare AI regulatory sandbox with three new pilots that could let AI produce care plans and medications without human review — the first US state to let an algorithm prescribe.
items.rationale: A dated regulatory decision by a named state regulator that moves the human-review line in prescribing — policy direction with an immediate practical consequence, and openly readable.

items.excerpt: AIRS Medical got FDA 510(k) clearance on Oct 5 for SwiftSight Body Composition, AI MRI software that quantifies visceral and subcutaneous fat, abdominal and thigh muscle and liver fat via proton density fat fraction.
items.rationale: A dated FDA 510(k) clearance with a named device and a specified measurement set — the regulatory-approval kind of contact, concrete enough to act on.

items.excerpt: An independent external validation of an AI model that reads dual-stain cytology for triage in HPV-based cervical cancer screening — the automation step that screening programs have been missing.
items.rationale: An independent external validation, the read-out that decides whether a screening program can adopt a model — the highest-credibility evidence tier in the pool.

items.excerpt: Twenty LLMs were given synthetic cases and records drawn from real clinical recommendations and asked to choose among two harmful and two safe actions, testing whether hospital-deployed models follow instructions that conflict with patient safety.
items.rationale: A measured patient-safety failure mode across 20 models, aimed at exactly the hospital deployments the other cards describe — the safety counterweight the section needs on day one.

dedup.note: First published day for the medicine section — news_data.json has no sections.medicine, so there is no in-section history and no history_digest; every pick is verdict 'new' with nearest ''. Per the orchestrator's instruction I did NOT dedup against other sections (zero URL overlap with the 239 published cards was verified upstream). Within-pool content dedup across the 15 surviving candidates: no two picks describe the same event. Two near-neighbour pairs were checked and split: (a) the two FDA clearances (AIRS Medical MRI body composition, AuntMinnie; pediatric bone age, Radiology Business) are different devices and different filings, so not duplicates — I kept only AIRS to avoid two clearance cards and to add a fifth outlet; (b) STAT 'FDA spells out 2027 AI guidance plans' and the Utah sandbox story are both regulator-direction items but different regulators and different actions — I kept Utah. DROPPED and why: STAT 'FDA 2027 AI guidance' (STAT+ paywall; same regulator-direction slot as Utah, which is concrete and open — Healthcare Dive's non-paywalled version of the FDA story was also available but is a second Healthcare Dive item and a weaker, forward-looking plan). STAT 'Claude analyzed my genome in 30 minutes' (STAT+ paywall plus first-person opinion; the capability claim is an anecdote, not a clinical read-out — keeping it would have put two paywalled cards in five). Radiology Business pediatric bone age clearance and Radiology Business acute-pancreatitis organ-failure model (both solid, but they would make three Radiology Business cards, over the 2-per-outlet cap; the pancreatitis item is also a single-centre model read-out weaker than the NEJM AI external validation). npj Digital Medicine Parkinson's telerehabilitation RCT (real trial, but self-described feasibility with exploratory signals, so a softer read-out than NEJM AI). Nature Medicine MedGemma open vision-language model (a model release benchmarked on medical images — 'AI got better at biology/medicine' with no patient, clinician or regulator contact; belongs in science by the section boundary in sources.json). Fierce Healthcare RFK Jr. physician backlash (reaction to a remark, no decision, filing or release). Healthcare Dive insurers-vs-billing-vendors cost dispute (real payer/liability angle, but duelling vendor-funded claims with no ruling; dropped last and would be the first substitute if a pick is swapped out). Healthcare Dive patient data-privacy survey (attitude survey, nothing reaches a patient) and MedCity News 'AI's Healthcare Doomsday' (contributed opinion with no verifiable capability, date or number) — both confirmed weakest, dropped as the collector flagged. SAFETY: nothing in the final five touches pathogen enhancement, gain-of-function or bioweapon design; all five are diagnostics, deployment, clearance or safety-evaluation items. Final-five spread: one live deployment, one state regulatory decision, one FDA clearance, one independent external validation, one patient-safety evaluation. Outlets: Radiology Business 1, Healthcare Dive 1, AuntMinnie 1, NEJM AI 1, Communications Medicine (Nature) 1 — five distinct outlets, no duplicate URLs, zero paywalled sources. All five share the single medicine category, so rank 1 keeps the category accent #00897b and ranks 2-5 take distinct accents from the sources.json palette; motif is the category's 'sphere'.
